claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. I have one child - Alex, who is 15 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Are you currently responsible for Alex? By this I mean, does Alex live with you and do you provide for their care (such as food, clothing, and general upkeep)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me full-time and I'm completely responsible for him. I provide everything - his food, clothes, school supplies, all his general care and upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I need to ask about Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** For example, is he attending school, college, or an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in school. He's doing his GCSEs at the moment - you know, the standard school curriculum for his age.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** For example, Alex's other parent or another person?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Do you have immigration permission or the right to reside in the UK?** In other words, are you a British citizen, have settled status, or have permission to be in the UK that would allow you to claim benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen, so I have the right to reside here and claim benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 15 years old and in full-time education (studying for GCSEs)
- You are responsible for Alex - he lives with you full-time and you provide all his care
- You live in the UK and are a British citizen
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit. You can now proceed to make a claim if you haven't already done so. If you need help with the application process, you can apply online through the government website or by post.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
